# Safe code review: WA-2462 workspace safe selector

**Mode:** you gave a committed range (`bcfe6bd…HEAD`), so only committed changes were reviewed. The range starts from the common ancestor `f09ce2c` and ends at `7c40c32`. That is 12 files, +685 −120, across 3 commits.
**Repo:** Safe{Wallet} web (Next.js, TypeScript, Jest). The written rules come from the root `AGENTS.md` and `apps/web/AGENTS.md`. All 9 review areas had something to check.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | **Fix one thing before opening the PR.** |
| **Score** | ~84/100 (2 of 6 findings checked by the prove/disprove agents) |
| **What held it down** | The warning about lookalike addresses is missing in the new workspace view |
| **Fix first** | #1: compute the similarity warnings before removing workspace safes from the list |

## Scores by area (worst first)

| Area | Score | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Security | 80 | #1 |
| Testing | 88 | #4, and a test that sets up an impossible state (#2) |
| KISS | 90 | #2 |
| Performance | 94 | #3 |
| Conventions | 94 | #5, #6 |
| Bugs · Regression · Architecture · DRY | 100 | Checked, nothing found |

## Must fix before opening

**#1 · P2 · Security: lookalike safes are not flagged in "Safes not in this workspace"** (both agents agree)
`apps/web/src/components/common/SpaceSafeBar/AccountsModal/useAccountsModalItems.ts:102`
- **What:** `getFlaggedSimilarAddressSet` only sees the list after workspace safes have been removed (`:89-92`).
- **Why it matters:** An attacker can deploy a Safe that lists the victim as an owner. It then comes back from CGW's owned-safes endpoint and shows up in this modal. If that Safe looks like one of the workspace safes, it gets no "High similarity" badge and no bold highlighting, because the safe it imitates was removed before the check ran.
- **Why it's new:** Before this change the modal couldn't be opened from a workspace (the footer was `undefined`). The new button at `SpaceSafeBar/index.tsx:171-182` opens it. No other check in the modal catches this: the badge is driven only by `similarAddresses`.
- **Fix:** Run the similarity check on the full list (unfiltered `allSafes` plus the workspace safes), then remove the workspace safes. Add a hook test where a non-workspace safe resembles a workspace safe. The docblock calls this a "known v1 limitation" (`:52-55`). That explains the gap, but it doesn't make it safe.

## Worth a ticket or a quick fix

| # | Pri | Area | Where | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | P3 | KISS | `useAccountsModalItems.ts:139` | **Confirmed by both agents.** The check `isQualifiedSafe && spaceSafesLoading` can never be true. `useIsQualifiedSafe` only returns true once `currentData` exists for the same `useSpaceSafesGetV1Query` (same args, same skip). RTK Query's `isLoading` is false as soon as that cache entry has data. So the flicker described in the comment at `:136-138` and in commit 7c40c32 can't happen. The test at `useAccountsModalItems.test.ts:87-95` mocks a combination the real hooks never produce. Remove the check and the test, or gate on something that can actually be missing. |
| 3 | P3 | Performance | `useAccountsModalItems.ts:71-74` | Not checked by agents. `useSpaceSafes` returns a new `allSafes` array on every render, because `safeItems` isn't memoized (`features/spaces/hooks/useSpaceSafes.tsx:29`). In a workspace, that means the exclusion set, filter, grouping, sort and similarity check all run again on every `SpaceSafeBar` render, even while the modal is closed. The hooks run before `if (!open)` at `AccountsModal/index.tsx:34`. The cost grows with how many safes the user has. |
| 4 | P3 | Testing | `useAccountsModalItems.test.ts` | Not checked by agents. The hook's tests never assert `similarAddresses`: neither which addresses get flagged nor which list the check runs on. The fix for #1 needs that test. The owned-safes error notification (the `showNotification` effect that moved into the hook) is also untested. |
| 5 | P3 | Conventions | `SpaceSafeBar/index.tsx:176`, `AccountsModal/index.tsx:42` | Not checked by agents. The new code uses the Title Case string "All Accounts". `AGENTS.md` requires sentence case ("All accounts"). The string already existed, but these lines are new. |
| 6 | P3 | Conventions | `useAccountsModalItems.ts:19-58` | Not checked by agents. The docblock is 40 lines, and `AGENTS.md` says to "treat code comments as tech debt". Part of it is already out of date: the similarity limitation (#1) and the loading comment (#2). Keep what #1 and #2 don't fix, and cut it down. |

## What this review didn't cover

- Only the two most disputable findings (#1, #2) went through the prove/disprove agents. #3–#6 are my own analysis and still count at full weight in the score.
- The review was read-only. I didn't run tests, type-check or lint, and I didn't check the UI in a browser.
- The nine areas were covered in one pass by me, not by nine separate category agents.
- There's no Storybook story for the new `DropdownWorkspaceHeader`, and `apps/web/AGENTS.md:10` asks for one for new components. It's a small inline sub-component, so I left it as a judgement call rather than a finding.

## Ruled out

- Address case when excluding workspace safes: both sides are lowercased (`:73`, `:91`), so matching is correct.
- Hiding the connect-wallet footer in a workspace (`index.tsx:172`): intended.
- Hiding the pin controls in the workspace modal: consistent throughout, and tested.

Nothing was posted or edited.
